newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, cash rate eases.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, cash rate eases.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen contract on TIFFE ended firmer on Friday in response to easier cash short-term rates, traders said.
The June ended at 99.27 after fluctuating in a range of 99.25-30, compared with Thursday's 99.26.
The three-month cash Euroyen rate fell to a quoted rate of 0.525-0.510 at 0716 GMT, down from Thursday's 0.530-0.520 percent.
The yield curve between the overnight rate and the one-year rate has flattened further, discouraging dealers' transactions aimed at taking profit from the yield spread.
The key overnight call rate was at 0.48 percent, unchanged from Friday. The one-year interest rate swap (IRS) rate was at 0.59-0.63 percent, down from 0.65-0.69 percent a week ago.

"Outstanding volume in the money market has been declining as the cash is shifting out into the long-term debt market due to a lack of sufficient profit opportunities in the short-end and a flattening of the short-term yield curve," a senior money trader said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 300 billion yen into the money market in the morning via its regular operation, which was neutral for the market.

Many traders say that the BOJ is unlikely to raise its official discount rate, which stands at a record-low 0.5 percent, before mid-1997 because it needs first to assess the deflationary impact on the economy of a planned hike in the consumption tax.
The consumption tax is scheduled to be raised to five percent from the current three percent from April 1, 1997.
One of the debt market focuses is on whether Japan will adopt an extra budget to stimulate its slow economy.
But traders said that at the moment they were not worried about a possible negative impact on rates from the supplementary budget.
Japan's Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said earlier this week that the three parties in the outgoing coalition had not made a decision about forming a supplementary budget this year.
"The supplementary budget is unlikely to materialised until perhaps December, judging from difficulty in forming a new coalition government," a city bank trader said.
